pr_body:
ATT channel sent callback shall not be overwritting until the
operation completes as it can result in breaking flow control when
CONFIG_BT_ATT_ENFORCE_FLOW is enabled.

Fixes #25964
Fixes #26070
Fixes #26071

Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
pr_comments: @alexsven could you check if your unsubscribe scenario under ATT traffic works now with this PR?

> @Vudentz thanks!
> 
> > Fixes #25964 #26071
> 
> You will need 2 separate `Fixes` lines for GitHub to pick up both issues

Done.
@Vudentz There should be 3 issues fixed now, right? Missing https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/26070

> @Vudentz I also ran into an issue where the error code was not forwarded to the user because of this:
> https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/host/att.c#L2833
> I'm not sure why the error code was ignored in this case, are there some other parts relying on the fact that it returns 0 here?

Right, Ive might have reverted with EATT but it should be returning the error there since we cannot queue when the cb is set.

> @Vudentz thanks!
> 
> > Fixes #25964 #26071
> 
> You will need 2 separate `Fixes` lines for GitHub to pick up both issues

Done.

> @Vudentz There should be 3 issues fixed now, right? Missing #26070

Done.

@carlescufi process_queue will not attempt to take tx_sem like bt_att_chan_send would, so it is essencially just taking ownership of the slot used by the previous request, iirc this was made like that to reduce the time we spend on the sent callback.
@Vudentz would you mind sending this PR against the `v2.3-branch` so we backport it in time for v2.3.1? Thanks!

Hi @Vudentz , thanks for quick response. I tested yours commit, it seems to solve ATT Request sending problem.

review_comments: In the ATT timeout handler the channel that the ATT timeout happened for will be detached, what about if you had other  ATT channels active at the same time? How would they be released?
Timeout is per bearer, other channels will not be affected, provided they don't timeout as well.

But you would call att_reset and notify gatt that the connection is disconnect, not the channel. Since att_reset is called the att->conn is set to NULL and bt_att_send will now return ENOTCONN for everything as far as I can tell.
Right. missed that.
@Vudentz In the line above it is checking for `if (chan->sent)`, should chan->sent be set to NULL afterwards then?
Agreed, this looks suspicious, is `chan->sent` being set to NULL elsewhere @Vudentz ?
That is just there because chan_cb can return NULL, reseting to NULL doesn't make any difference here since chan_send will always attempt to set the callback when called.
